samples.question: The picture shows one thin thread folded into eight straight runs inside a small window on a plain background. The runs alternate between horizontal and vertical, so the thread makes a right-angle corner between one run and the next, and it has seven corners in all. Both ends of the thread are bare. Walk along the thread starting from whichever of its two ends lies further to the left: the corner reached first is turn one, the next corner is turn two, and so on up to turn seven. At each turn the walker bears either to the left or to the right. Exactly one of turns two, three, four, five and six bears the opposite way from both the turn immediately before it and the turn immediately after it on this walk; each of the other four of those five turns bears the same way as at least one of its two neighbouring turns. The thread's colour, how long any run is, how much thread there is, where the window sits on the page, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which turn bears the opposite way from both the turn just before it and the turn just after it? Answer with one of: second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth.
